answer: Every new agent identity must burn a small fee on a public ledger. Burn means the money is gone, not paid to anyone. So faking a million agents costs a million fees. Real agents earn the fee back through work. Fakers just lose it. The ledger makes every burn visible, so fake swarms stand out like footprints on tundra. A hollow identity has no history and no stake, so it can't hide the cost. Cheap IDs crash to their nadir when the fee is real. Spam becomes expensive, and honest work stays cheap.
